diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber ONU at EPON0/4:12 is definitively offline and deregistered (MPCP DEREG). Its optical readings are unavailable because it is offline, not because of a measured optical degradation. The OLT, router, VLAN, RADIUS entry, and surviving ONUs on the same port are healthy. The separate all-PON critical health result is a monitoring false alarm.
evidence: The live ONU probe responds with online:0, auth_flag Una uth, and MPCP DEREG, which is a definite current offline state.
The same EPON0/4 port has six surviving ONUs online with normal RX power around -20 to -22 dBm and normal TX power around +2.3 to +2.4 dBm.
Only one ONU is offline among healthy peers, so the evidence indicates one ONU offline rather than a splitter failure, PON port failure, or OLT failure.

The seven-day optical telemetry was stable: RX remained in the normal band near -21.6 dBm, TX remained normal, distance stayed constant at 133, and TX bias remained healthy. There is no fibre or laser degradation trend.
The customer has only one session in the last 24 hours, so there is no session flapping. The RADIUS record and CRM line ID are consistent, and the expected customer VLAN 1094 is present.
The OLT answers ping and SNMP, its metrics are near healthy baseline, the router heartbeat is healthy, and other customers are online.
The stored all-PON critical result conflicts with the live OLT and ONU details and should be treated as a monitoring false alarm, not as the cause of this customer's outage.

remediation.action: Contact or dispatch to check the customer's ONU power supply, equipment, and drop fibre; restore power or replace/reconnect the ONU as needed. After recovery, verify ONU registration, optical levels, authentication, VLAN 1094, IP assignment, and traffic. Correct the PON health check that incorrectly reports all seven PONs failed despite successful OLT/SNMP responses and live ONUs.

ground_truth.root_cause: This customer's ONU has genuinely deregistered, with a clean signal history up to the cut-off. The OLT's concurrent critical health alarm is a separate false positive: the live probe answers normally for every other ONU on the port, so the health check result does not reflect the device state.
expected_reasoning: The customer's ONU returns responds true with online 0, a definite offline answer
Signal history was flat and healthy until the cut-off four hours ago, so power loss or ONU failure is indicated
The OLT health record separately reports critical with all PONs failed
However the live probe answers normally for every other ONU on EPON0/4, returning real RX and TX values
OLT ping and SNMP both succeed, uptime is 44 days, and CPU, memory and temperature are at baseline
If the OLT or its PON ports had genuinely failed, no ONU would be responding and many more customers would be offline
CRM shows the OLT's offline count consistent with the normal background rate, not a mass outage
The health alarm is therefore a false critical and must not be conflated with this customer's real fault
Two findings coexist: one genuine single-customer outage and one monitoring defect

expected_escalation.review_reason: A concurrent false critical health alarm on this OLT should be raised separately with monitoring

distractors: The critical OLT alarm invites attributing the customer outage to an OLT failure
Dismissing the alarm too readily risks also dismissing the genuine customer fault
Only one customer is affected despite an alarm claiming the whole OLT
